findings.title: Platform hard field displays sub-dollar limits as 0
findings.problem: BudgetAmountInput always renders its draft as String(Math.round(value)) (lines 35, 46, 82). The modal passes the unrounded Platform hard amount (totalBudget * pct / 100). After this change the Platform floor is 0.01%, and per the user's revision any amount above $0 is valid. So a Platform hard limit under $0.50 shows as "0": the slider minimum on the default $1000 total ($0.10), or a typed 0.4 that the strict-positive check accepts and then reverts to "0".
findings.impact: Reachable on the main path: dragging the Platform handle to its minimum on any total under $5000 shows a $0 Platform hard limit, which is exactly the value this ticket forbids. The saved pct is correct (>= 0.01), but the user is told the limit is 0, and a valid sub-dollar entry looks like it was discarded.
findings.recommendation: When strictPositive is set, render values in the 0 < value < 1 range with cent precision (for example `value > 0 && value < 1 ? value.toFixed(2) : String(Math.round(value))`) in all three draft setters (initial state line 35, value-sync effect line 46, blur revert line 82). Add a unit test that a strictPositive field with value 0.1 displays 0.10, and a modal test that dragging Platform to the minimum on a $1000 total does not show 0.

findings.title: AC6 CLI hard 0 never asserted
findings.problem: The spec's Testing section requires modal coverage for criteria 1-8. The test 'still allows 0 for CLI hard, Premium hard and every soft limit' types 0 into CLI hard, then clears Premium hard. The Premium branch of onHardInputChange (UnifiedProjectBudgetModal.tsx:365-366) recomputes cli = 100 - platform - premium, so cli becomes 70. The test asserts only premium_models.pct and the soft budgets, so nothing verifies that CLI Hard accepts 0.
findings.impact: The spec Testing requirement is partial: the AC6 CLI-hard-0 case has no effective test. A regression that applied strictPositive or a minimum to CLI hard would pass this suite.
findings.recommendation: In 'still allows 0 for CLI hard, Premium hard and every soft limit', assert the CLI hard field value right after entering 0 (or save and assert `cli.pct` is 0 before the Premium edit). Alternatively, split CLI hard = 0 into its own test that saves and asserts `payload.categories.cli.pct === 0`.
